title: finding(tests): whole-corpus walks inside the 15s testTimeout are green on every PR and red on every push — two instances 12 hours apart, each silencing the coverage gate
body:
## Observation

Two test files have now crossed vitest's 15 s `testTimeout` in the **push lane only**, twelve hours apart, and the repair was the same both times: hoist a whole-corpus walk out of the timed window.

| when | file | card | fix |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 2026-09-07T21:43Z | `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-links.test.ts` | objectui#8419 | `ANCHOR_CORPUS` at module scope (`0203a29e9`) |
| 2026-09-08 (in flight) | `scripts/__tests__/check-unused-dependencies.test.ts` | objectui#8479 | `REPOSITORY_SCAN` at module scope (PR #8543) |

⇒ Two instances is a shape, not a coincidence — and the second one held `main`'s coverage gate unevaluated for **84 consecutive runs** before anyone read the name.

## ⭐ Why PR CI structurally cannot see this class

The two lanes run the **same** 4-way shard split over the **same** files. The only difference is that the push lane adds v8 coverage instrumentation. Measured on objectui#8479's branch, same tree, same shard:

- `--project unit … --shard=1/4` **without** `--coverage`: exit 0, 682 files passed.
- the same shard **with** `--coverage`: exit 1, three tests `Test timed out in 15000ms`.

⇒ A file whose walk fits inside 15 s uninstrumented and does not fit instrumented is **green on every PR and red on every push**. ⛔ No amount of PR CI discipline surfaces it; it is only ever discovered after it is already on `main`.

⚠️ And the discovery is expensive out of proportion to the defect: the coverage thresholds live only on the **merged** 4-shard report (the shard legs override them to zero), so **one** red shard means the coverage gate does not run at all. A per-test timeout in one file silences a whole quality gate.

## The population at risk, measured rather than guessed

Slowest survivors in `Test (coverage shard 1/4)` under coverage, measured by the objectui#8479 dev:

```
scripts/__tests__/unit-registry-absence-collision.test.ts   46798 ms / 15 tests
scripts/__tests__/check-vi-mock-inherit.test.ts             20852 ms / 86 tests
scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-en-drift.test.ts               13860 ms / 37 tests
```

⚠️ ⛔ **None of these crosses the per-test bound today** — those are file-level totals, not single-assertion times, and no claim is made that any of them is about to fail. What the numbers say is that the margin is thin in a family of files that all share one shape: a whole-corpus walk (`git ls-files`, every manifest, every doc) driven from inside an `it()`.

⚠️ Also not established: whether the shard a given file lands in is stable. It is not — objectui#8479 measured the failing shard oscillating between 2, 1, and both as the file list grew, because shard membership is a function of the sorted file list. ⇒ A file can move across the bound without anyone editing it.

## Two shapes a fix could take, ⛔ neither proposed as a ruling

1. **A convention**, stated once and enforced by a gate: a test that walks the whole corpus computes it at module scope, ⛔ not inside `it()` and ⛔ not in `beforeAll` (which trades the 15 s `testTimeout` for the narrower `hookTimeout` default). Both existing repairs already take exactly this shape, so the convention would be describing what the tree does rather than inventing a rule.
2. **Make the class visible where it is created**: some reading in the PR lane that would flag a test whose instrumented cost approaches the bound. ⚠️ This is the harder half and may not be cheap — the honest version needs the coverage-instrumented timing, which is the thing PR CI does not run.

⭐ The load-bearing point is ⛔ neither of those: it is that **the second instance was found by reading a job log after 84 red pushes**, and the first was found the same way. A class that can only be discovered post-hoc, one instance at a time, at the cost of a silenced gate each time, is worth a convention even if the convention is only a sentence.

## Provenance and dedupe

Measured by the `os-dev` seat working objectui#8479 and handed to the PM seat **explicitly as out of scope** rather than filed there — the seat wrote that closing the class *"would close the class rather than the instance — PM's call, and out of scope here."*

Dedupe: 600 raw rows pulled by repo-scoped REST (`state=all`, newest first, **paginated on raw page length**), 331 non-PR issues, grepped locally for `timeout|timed out|testTimeout|coverage lane|hoist`. Three title hits: objectui#8380 (**open** — the same *instance* as objectui#8479, same file, same assertion; ⛔ not the class), objectui#8404 (closed, host-dependent tests), objectui#7956 (closed, missing `timeout-minutes` on jobs). ⛔ None is this. Presence controls in the same fetched set: objectui#8541, objectui#8479 and objectui#8465 all present.

⛔ This card asserts no priority and no domain — filed for triage's first grading. `finding` only: nothing is broken today, and the two known instances are both already repaired.
